sources.entry: Medusa - Automatic Video library manager for TV Shows. It watches for new episodes of your favorite shows, and when they are posted it does its magic. (Clients) GPL-3.0 Python

summary.one_liner: Medusa is a self-hosted automatic video library manager for TV shows that monitors configured shows, searches Usenet and torrent providers, sends releases to download clients, and organizes completed episodes.
summary.what_it_does: Medusa fetches show metadata from a selected indexer (TVDBv2, TVmaze, TMDB, or IMDb), runs scheduled and manual searches across configured torrent and Usenet providers, and sends the chosen release to an external download client. After download it renames, sorts, and enriches episodes with posters, NFO files, and subtitles, then updates Kodi, Plex, or Emby. It also supports backlog, proper, and repack searches, season packs, anime parsing via GuessIt and AniDB, and Trakt import and sync. Notifications go to services such as Discord, Slack, Telegram, and Pushover.
use_cases: Automatically download new episodes of TV shows
Manage a TV show library with renaming and sorting
Search and snatch specific episodes or season packs
Organize anime libraries with release-group filters
Download and match subtitles for TV episodes
Update Kodi, Plex, or Emby after downloads
how_to_run: docker pull pymedusa/medusa:latest (or use the Docker Compose example in the README, mapping port 8081)
notable: Covers the full pipeline from indexer metadata through search, download client, post-processing, and media server
Supports Usenet (SABnzbd, NZBGet) and many torrent clients (qBittorrent, Transmission, Deluge, and others)
Anime-specific parsing, AniDB mappings, and release-group white/blacklists
Manual search shows provider, quality, seeders, and release details before snatching
Official Docker image for linux/amd64, arm/v7, and arm64
caveats: Requires external torrent or Usenet providers and a compatible download client; it does not supply content
Source install needs Python 3.10 or later; some older wiki platform guides may be outdated
Community NAS packages are maintained outside the main repository
